  "text": "The dentist found a key beneath my tongue.

“Have you swallowed anything unusual?” she asked.

I shook my head.

She held it under the lamp. Small, black, with a thread of pink tissue caught between its teeth.

“Well,” she said, “it's been there a while.”

That night, I discovered a keyhole in the bathroom mirror.

It appeared only when I breathed on the glass.

I called the dentist. Her voicemail said the practice had closed in 1986.

The key lay beside my toothbrush.

By morning, it was warm.

I should have thrown it away. Instead, I steamed the mirror with the shower and pushed the key into the little dark opening.

It turned easily.

The mirror swung inward.

Behind it was another bathroom, identical to mine except for the muddy shoes beneath the sink.

My mother's shoes.

She had been buried barefoot because we couldn't find them.

Someone coughed beyond the other bathroom door.

“Mum?”

The coughing stopped.

A piece of paper slid beneath the door.

I recognized her handwriting before I read it.

PUT IT BACK UNDER YOUR TONGUE.

The doorknob began to turn.

I pulled the mirror shut, locked it, and placed the key in my mouth.

Immediately, skin tightened around it.

From the other side of the glass came my mother's relieved sigh.

Then her voice, very close.

“Good. Now don't let the next one take it.”

This morning, my dentist called to confirm an appointment.

I told her I wasn't coming.

“I know,” she said. “I'm outside.”"
